construct: ATP2C1 encodes hSPCA1, an ATP-powered pump that transports calcium and manganese into the Golgi apparatus. Loss of functional hSPCA1 disrupts Golgi calcium storage in keratinocytes, impairing cell adhesion and making the epidermis fragile in areas exposed to heat, moisture, and friction.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: ATP2C1 encodes hSPCA1, an ATP-powered secretory-pathway pump that transports calcium, and also manganese, into the Golgi apparatus. Loss of this function impairs keratinocyte calcium homeostasis and adhesion in Hailey-Hailey disease.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: ATP-dependent calcium transport into the endoplasmic reticulum describes SERCA pumps, not ATP2C1/hSPCA1. Plasma-membrane calcium channels and sodium-calcium exchange have different locations and energetics, and ER-to-Golgi protein trafficking is vesicular rather than the ATP2C1 ion-pump function.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The gene is explicitly ATP2C1, so Golgi calcium transport by hSPCA1 is the uniquely correct cellular function.
